name: L-Sit Progression
description: A calisthenics isometric hold where the body is supported on the hands with the legs extended horizontally, forming an L-shape. The L-sit builds extraordinary hip flexor and core strength, tricep pushing endurance, and shoulder girdle stability simultaneously. Progressions range from tuck holds through full L-sit.

execution.starting_position: Support your body weight on two parallel bars or the floor with arms fully extended beneath you. Legs are extended forward parallel to the floor.
execution.setup_instructions: Use parallettes, the floor, or gymnastics rings. Ensure the support surface is at a height allowing the legs to extend without touching the floor.
steps: Step 1 (Tuck): Support the body on hands with knees pulled to chest. Hold for time.
Step 2 (Single-leg): Extend one leg while tucking the other. Alternate.
Step 3 (Full L-sit): Extend both legs forward parallel to the floor. Hold for maximum time.
Step 4: Lower controlled and rest before the next set.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe steadily throughout the hold. Do not hold your breath.
common_mistakes: Allowing the hips to drop below the support — the hips must be at or above handle height
safety_considerations: Build wrist and elbow strength before attempting this exercise
Progress through the tuck stages before the full version
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Legs parallel to the floor. Arms fully extended. Body in an L-shape.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Isometric hold — build to 3 sets of 10-30 seconds
coaching_cues: Point the toes and squeeze the quads
